language.sample_text: この先工事中 — 注意
language.script_notes: This is the highest-density, highest-coverage part of the whole country, so most 'generic Japan' imagery is actually Honshu.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Plain white guardrail is the default; regional colour accents appear near prefecture borders (this file covers the un-accented central majority).
road_furniture.curb_style: Low concrete kerb with narrow drainage gutter — extremely common on residential streets in this densely built region.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Yellow-and-black striped poles nationwide; dense overhead wire clutter is especially pronounced here given how built-up the region is.

architecture.roof_style: Grey ceramic-tiled pitched roofs on older houses; flat-roofed apartment blocks and narrow multi-story urban houses dominate Tokyo/Osaka/Nagoya.
architecture.roof_material: Grey kawara ceramic tile classic; flat concrete/asphalt roofing on city apartment blocks.
architecture.wall_construction: Extremely narrow multi-story houses packed onto tiny lots, especially in and around Tokyo and Osaka; traditional wooden machiya townhouses in old Kyoto/Kanazawa neighbourhoods.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Muted grey/beige with dense overhead wiring; the traditional wooden brown of machiya houses in historic districts.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Dense multi-story urban housing, konbini on nearly every block, vending machines everywhere, train stations and level crossings, Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples, Kyoto's traditional machiya streets.

nature.vegetation: Dense cedar/cypress-forested mountains surrounding flat, intensively built coastal plains; rice paddies fill any remaining open valley land.
nature.terrain: Central mountainous spine (the Japanese Alps) with population and roads squeezed into narrow coastal plains — Tokyo/Kanto plain and Kansai (Osaka/Kyoto/Kobe) plain are the two largest flat areas.
nature.climate_signature: Humid subtropical to humid continental; green most of the year, occasional snow inland/north side in winter.

vehicles.plate_format: Top line shows a Honshu regional office name — e.g. 品川/練馬 (Tokyo wards), なにわ/大阪 (Osaka), 名古屋 (Nagoya).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Kei cars everywhere given how narrow the streets are; heavy taxi and delivery-van presence in the big cities.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mix of Gen 3 and Gen 4, with the newest coverage concentrated in and around the largest cities.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: The densest and most complete coverage in the whole country — this is the 'default' Japan look most players see.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same script, same plate style, similar narrow-street urban housing
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Honshu lacks Kyushu's green-banded guardrails and Yamaguchi's orange 'natsumikan' guardrails, and lacks Okinawa's red-tiled roofs and shisa statues; Honshu's terrain is generally more mountainous-and-squeezed than Kyushu's.
Honshu's roads are narrower and its terrain more mountainous/built-up than Hokkaido's wide, snow-adapted roads and flat agricultural plains.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Dense East Asian city streets, similar overhead-wire clutter
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Japan drives on the left with kanji/hiragana/katakana mixed script; Korea drives on the right with Hangul.
